thesis.core: PetroChina has durable integrated upstream, refining, marketing and gas assets with large positive operating cash flow and shareholder distributions. Its 2026 nine-month profit improvement is real, but partly reflects elevated oil prices rather than a durable step-up in through-cycle returns. A-share price already capitalizes an optimistic commodity scenario; new capital is justified only after a fresh valuation margin and portfolio energy-exposure check.
thesis.variant_wedge: 2026 9M attributable profit RMB155.773bn +21.9% and deducted attributable profit RMB158.899bn +23.7%; operating cash RMB373.539bn +8.8% and cash capex RMB159.440bn leave indicative pre-dividend operating cash less capex RMB214.099bn, not fully attributable equity FCF. 2026 H1 Brent averaged around USD87.60/bbl and 2026 9M Brent about USD88.86/bbl, so annualizing 9M EPS mechanically would overstate normalized cycle earnings. 2026 consolidation of three storage entities led to prior-year restatement; compare adjusted figures.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: 2026 9M basic EPS RMB0.85; 2025 full-year EPS RMB0.86 and 2025 9M restated EPS RMB0.70 imply 2025 Q4 about RMB0.16, so simple trailing 12-month EPS roughly RMB1.01. Through-cycle common EPS modeled RMB0.80-1.15 with base RMB0.95 to reflect commodity-price normalization, refining/gas resilience, capex and minority interests. These are analyst scenarios, not issuer guidance.

operating_and_financial_quality.judgment: Cash generation and integrated scale pass business-quality screening. However the 2026 oil-price upcycle and valuation premium require normalized earnings rather than annualized peak EPS. Cash flow less capex is a rough pre-dividend group proxy, not free cash distributable to A-shareholders after all debt, leases, working capital and minority interests. Oil-price, downstream demand, geopolitical and energy-transition risks remain material.

normalized_earnings_basis.rationale: 2026 oil-price gains are cyclical; 9M annualized EPS about RMB1.13 is not used as a perpetual run rate. Base RMB0.95 is an analyst midcycle assumption; scenario PE 9-13x embeds uncertainty about future Brent, refining margins, gas demand and required reinvestment. H-share discount is not mechanically imported into A-share value.

catalysts: Sustained gas-sales margin and chemical-product profitability support normalized EPS despite a retreat from 2026 elevated oil prices.
Positive group operating cash after cash capex persists and dividends are supported by recurring, not windfall, cash generation.
Oil-price normalization lowers market valuation toward formal entry hurdle without a corresponding structural deterioration in asset quality.
Incremental integrated gas and storage returns prove attractive without an excessive capital spending cycle.
kill_thesis: Brent and realized oil prices normalize while recurring upstream cash margins fall below midcycle assumptions and group CFO cannot cover maintenance and committed growth capex.
Refining and marketing profitability structurally weakens due to fuel demand displacement, impairments or price-control pressure.
Material deterioration in group leverage, dividend coverage or minority-interest leakage reduces cash distributable to common shareholders.
A material increase in required capex or asset impairments undermines the modeled normalized common EPS range.

evidence_gap.monitoring: 2026Q3 is unaudited; oil-cycle normalized earnings and valuation multiples are explicit analyst assumptions.
